Dataset: 1345 drugs from dataset3, each one name-matched to ChEMBL and then standardised with RDKit — largest fragment, neutralised, metals refused.
Routing target: ChEMBL's mechanism-of-action table, filtered on parent_molecule_chembl_id. 683 of them carry a primary target and can be routed at all.

Training data: one ChEMBL set per target, 35 targets, 58,260 cleaned compound/activity pairs. One standard_type per target (never Ki and IC50 mixed), binding assays only, exact relations only, duplicates merged by median, replicates spanning more than one log unit dropped.
Predictors: 16 declared whole-molecule descriptors, fixed before any model was fitted — mw, clogp, clogp_sq, mr, tpsa, hbd, hba, rotb and 8 more.
Measured human PK from dataset3 (fu, Vdss, clearance, MRT, half-life) travels with every row under a measured_ prefix and is never fitted against. It is a measurement, not a descriptor.

Output: one CSV. One column per predictor, therapeutic index last. 144 rows carry an index; the remaining 1201 are in the file with an empty index and a stated reason, the largest being “no primary target in ChEMBL's mechanism table” (662).
Workflow: Endpoint (OECD 1): p_toxicity(hERG, CHEMBL240) - p_activity(primary target), both -log10 mol/L. Higher is a wider margin over the cardiac liability. This is not LD50/ED50, not a clinical therapeutic index, not dose-aware, not safety evidence.

Conditional routing: a molecule's activity is only ever predicted from a model trained on its own primary target. There is no fallback to another target — if that target has no usable model the row is left empty with a reason. The toxicity side always comes from hERG (CHEMBL240).

Two tiers per target, in order. 1. Measurement, where ChEMBL has one. 2. A Hansch equation for the congeneric series the molecule belongs to. 3. A declared non-linear fallback on the same descriptors, labelled non-mechanistic.

A molecule reaches a series equation only by belonging to that series: median Morgan Tanimoto at or above that series' own membership floor, the 10th percentile of its internal pairwise similarity. Exact scaffold matching was tried first and was wrong — it refused true camptothecins that differed from the series by one ring nitrogen.

Acceptance (OECD 4): series — n ≥ 15, median similarity ≥ 0.55, r² ≥ 0.6, q²(leave-one-out) ≥ 0.5, shuffled q² < 0.05. Terms capped at n/5 and chosen on AICc, so the criterion selected on is never the criterion reported.
Result: 53 of 543 candidate series passed; 28 of 35 targets produced a usable fallback, q² 0.25–0.68 with whole chemical families held out.
Applicability domain (OECD 3): descriptor range for a series equation, kNN distance at the 95th percentile for the fallback. 68 ranked rows sit inside it; the rest say so in their own row.
Software: RDKit: standardisation (LargestFragmentChooser, Uncharger), Crippen logP and molar refractivity, TPSA, QED, Gasteiger partial charges, Bemis–Murcko scaffolds, Morgan fingerprints at radius 2.
scikit-learn: the declared non-linear fallback (random forest, 300 trees) and the standardiser behind the kNN applicability domain. Nothing else.

Ordinary least squares, leave-one-out q², AICc and the y-randomisation test are written out in ti/fit.py rather than imported, so every figure in the report can be traced to the line that computed it.
Data sources: ChEMBL web API (activities, mechanisms, structures) and dataset3 for the batch and its measured human PK. No PubChem structures.

Reproducibility: ti/resolve.py → ti/pull_training.py → ti/fit.py --all → ti/rank.py → ti/report.py. Every stage caches, the random seed is fixed, and audit.json carries the input hashes and library versions that produced the CSV.
